Ancient History.Prehistoric India:
INTRODUCTION
Prehistory refers to the period before the invention of writing. Knowledge about this phase is derived from archaeological sources such as tools, pottery, bones and cave paintings. It is broadly divided into Paleolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic phases.

PALEOLITHIC AGE
This is the earliest phase of human history and is also known as the Old Stone Age. It extended from about 2.5 million years ago to around 10000 BCE.

FEATURES
• Use of crude stone tools such as hand axes and choppers
• Humans were hunter gatherers and depended on nature
• No permanent settlements and life was nomadic
• Discovery of fire was a major milestone in later stages
• Important sites include Bhimbetka, Hunsgi and Kurnool caves

MESOLITHIC AGE
This is the Middle Stone Age and represents a transitional phase between Paleolithic and Neolithic. It roughly dates from 10000 BCE to 6000 BCE.

FEATURES
• Use of microliths or small stone tools
• Beginning of semi permanent settlements
• Domestication of animals started
• Evidence of burials indicating belief systems
• Important sites include Bagor and Adamgarh

NEOLITHIC AGE
This is the New Stone Age and marks the beginning of food production. It roughly dates from 6000 BCE to 2000 BCE in India.

FEATURES
• Practice of agriculture and domestication of animals
• Use of polished stone tools
• Beginning of permanent settlements
• Development of pottery and weaving
• Important sites include Mehrgarh, Burzahom and Chirand

SIGNIFICANCE
• Transition from food gathering to food production
• Foundation for settled life and village communities
• Beginning of technological advancements like pottery and tools
• Development of social structures and early belief systems

IMPORTANT POINTS
• Bhimbetka is famous for rock paintings and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
• Mehrgarh is one of the earliest agricultural sites in the Indian subcontinent
• Neolithic phase marks the beginning of economic and social transformation

CONCLUSION
Prehistoric India laid the foundation for later civilizations. The gradual development from hunting gathering to agriculture and settlement marks one of the most important transitions in human history.
